sentences.text: This writ petition has been filed to direct the 1st respondent to conduct the inquiry and to cancel the contract of the 3rd respondent in pursuant to the proceedings Na.Ka.No.Aa7/0520/2025 dated 29.01.2025 issued by the 1st respondent.

2. The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that lease agreement has been forged, in this regard a police compliant was also given and FIR was also registered in Chindatripet Police Station in Cr.No.324 of 2024.
The learned counsel further submits that initially the petitioner had given the property on lease to run a shop in the name and style Suguna Motors for running motor repair centre.

According to the agreement dated 02.06.2002, the rent was fixed at Rs.45,000/- p.m., after entering into the agreement, the 3rd respondent taken the contract from the 1st respondent office for annual maintenance of machines.
As per the agreement, the lease period expires on 31.11.2023.

After the expiry of the rental agreement, the petitioner called upon the 3rd respondent for extended or renewal of the agreement, but the 3rd respondent replied that he is ready to vacate the premises.

The learned counsel would further submit that coming to know https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis (
Uploaded on: 17/03/2025 11:51:04 am ) that the contract has been renewed by the 1st respondent on 06.01.2025, immediately he had given representation before the first respondent on 23.01.2025,
which has not been considered till date.
Hence, the writ petition.

3. The learned Government Advocate appearing for the 2nd respondent would submit that based on the private complaint given by the petitioner under Section 173(3) BNSS before the XIV Metropolitan Magistrate, Egmore and the complaint was taken up on file in a case in Crl.MP.No.52483 of 2024 and the same was allowed by an order dated 14.11.2024, directing the 2nd respondent to register the case against the 3rd respondent.

Pursuant to the order dated 14.11.2024,
a case has been registered by the 2nd respondent against the 3rd respondent in Cr.No.324 of 2024 for the offences under Sections 406, 420, 465, 471 IPC on the file of the F1 - Chindathripet Police Station.

4. The learned Additional Government Pleader appearing for the first respondent submitted that the 3rd respondent had obtained an anticipatory bail from this Court in Crl.OP.No.31729 of 2024 dated 06.01.2025.
He further submitted that the suit has been filed by the 3rd respondent in https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
( Uploaded on: 17/03/2025 11:51:04 am ) OS.No.1010 of 2025 on the file of XII City Civil Court, Chennai.
He would further submit that contract was renewed by the first respondent in favour of the Suguna Motors (3rd respondent herein).

5. Heard the rival submissions made on either side and perused the materials documents available on record.
